props.title: St. Agatha

sections.content: **St. Agatha (2018)** (2018) stands as a haunting entry in the nunsploitation subgenre, following the dark tradition of films like The Devils (1971) and Dark Waters (1993). Set in 1957 Georgia, it tackles religious horror through the lens of a pregnant con woman seeking refuge in a convent that harbors sinister secrets. Director Darren Lynn Bousman, known for several **Saw** franchise entries (2005-2007), brings his expertise in visceral horror to this period piece, creating a claustrophobic atmosphere that recalls the psychological tension of Rosemary's Baby (1968).

sections.content: The nunsploitation subgenre emerged in the 1970s with provocative films like **School of the Holy Beast** (1974) and **Flavia the Heretic** (1974). These exploitation films often mixed religious imagery with horror and sexuality, challenging institutional authority. Modern interpretations like **The Nun** (2018) and **St. Agatha** take a more psychological approach, focusing on power dynamics and institutional abuse rather than explicit exploitation elements. SUBHEAD: Religious Horror Evolution

Religious horror has evolved significantly since **The Exorcist** (1973) defined the genre. Modern entries like **Saint Maud** (2019) and **The Witch** (2015) explore faith-based horror through a more nuanced lens, examining personal crisis and institutional corruption. **St. Agatha** bridges these approaches, combining traditional convent horror with contemporary psychological themes and body horror elements reminiscent of **Martyrs** (2008).
